name: iOS
metaTitle: iOS App Privacy Policy Generator — App Store Guideline 5.1.1 | PrivacyPage
metaDescription: What Apple requires: a privacy policy URL in App Store Connect and in the app, App Privacy answers that match it, and a privacy manifest for required-reason APIs. Sources cited.
answer: Every iOS app on the App Store needs a public privacy policy URL, entered in App Store Connect and linked inside the app (App Review Guideline 5.1.1). The policy must match your App Privacy answers in App Store Connect and the data your SDKs collect, including anything declared in a PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy privacy manifest.

storeRule.title: App Review Guideline 5.1.1(i) — Privacy Policies
storeRule.quote: All apps must include a link to their privacy policy in the App Store Connect metadata field and within the app in an easily accessible manner.

additionalRules.title: App Privacy answers (the “nutrition label”) must cover third-party code
additionalRules.text: In App Store Connect you answer what data your app collects, whether it is linked to the user, and whether it is used for tracking. Apple says you must include “the practices of third-party partners whose code you integrate into your app”, and the answers are required to submit new apps and updates. Your privacy policy should describe the same data — a policy that says “we collect nothing” next to a label listing Analytics and Identifiers is a mismatch reviewers and users can see. App Store Connect’s help repeats it: “You must include information about your app's privacy practices and those of third-party partners whose code you integrate into your app.”

additionalRules.title: Privacy policy URL is a required field
additionalRules.text: App Store Connect: “A privacy policy URL is required for all apps, while a user privacy choices URL is optional.” Changes to the URL are not instant: “Any changes to the URLs releases with your next app version.”

additionalRules.title: Privacy manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy)
additionalRules.text: Apps and third-party SDKs can ship a privacy manifest that records the types of data they collect and the required-reason APIs they use. Certain SDKs on Apple’s list must include a signed manifest. Treat the manifests in your dependencies as an input to both your App Privacy answers and your policy.

additionalRules.title: Required-reason APIs
additionalRules.text: Some APIs can be misused for fingerprinting, so you must declare an approved reason for each category you (or an SDK) use. Apple: “Starting May 1, 2024, apps that don’t describe their use of required reason API in their privacy manifest file aren’t accepted by App Store Connect.”

whereToPaste: Answer the privacy questions: App Store Connect → Apps → your app → App Privacy (sidebar) → Get Started. Say whether you or your third-party partners collect data, select every data type (including what your SDKs collect), answer the questions for each, then click Publish.
Add the policy URL: App Privacy (sidebar) → Edit next to Privacy Policy → enter the privacy policy URL → Save. It is required for all apps.
URL changes release with your next app version, so update it before you submit that version.
Inside the app: a Settings or About link that opens the same URL (Guideline 5.1.1(i)).

sampleClause.heading: Crash and diagnostic data
sampleClause.text: When the app crashes, we use Firebase Crashlytics (Google) to receive a crash trace and an installation identifier so we can find and fix the bug. This data is not used to track you across other companies’ apps or websites. It is listed under “Diagnostics” in our App Store privacy details.

faqs.q: Do I need a privacy policy if my iOS app collects no data?
faqs.a: Yes. Guideline 5.1.1(i) says all apps must link a privacy policy, and App Store Connect says a privacy policy URL is required for all apps. A short policy that truthfully says what the app does not collect is fine.

faqs.q: Does the policy have to match my App Privacy answers?
faqs.a: It should. Both describe the same data practices, including third-party SDKs. If they disagree, one of them is wrong — fix the one that does not reflect the app.

faqs.q: Is the privacy manifest the same as the privacy policy?
faqs.a: No. PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is a file inside your app bundle for Apple’s tooling. The privacy policy is a public web page for people. Both should describe the same data.
